citations.quote:
Let $(I,\Sigma,\gamma,k,a)$ be an FLRW model datum with conversion constant
$c>0$, with spacetime $M=I\times\Sigma$, metric $g$ and comoving congruence
$n=c^{-1}\partial_t$ ([[def-gr-flrw-model-data]]), and let $\nabla$ be the
metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Let
$(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ be a product chart with $x^0=t$, where $(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ is
a smooth chart of $\Sigma$, and let ${}^{(3)}\Gamma^i{}_{jk}$ be the Christoffel symbols of
the Riemannian metric $\gamma$ in that three-dimensional chart
([[prop-christoffel-formula-for-the-levi-civita-connection]]). Write
$\dot a$ for the derivative of the scale factor and $H=\dot a/a$ for the
Hubble parameter. Then in the product chart the Christoffel symbols
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) are:

**(a)** $\Gamma^0{}_{00}=\Gamma^0{}_{0i}=\Gamma^0{}_{i0}=0$ and
$\Gamma^i{}_{00}=0$ for $i=1,2,3$;

**(b)** $\Gamma^0{}_{ij}=\Gamma^0{}_{ji}=\dfrac{a\dot a}{c^2}\,\gamma_{ij}$
for $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$;

**(c)** $\Gamma^i{}_{0j}=\Gamma^i{}_{j0}=H\,\delta^i{}_j$ for
$i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$;

**(d)** $\Gamma^i{}_{jk}={}^{(3)}\Gamma^i{}_{jk}$ for
$i,j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$.

All components not listed vanish; equivalently, the only potentially nonzero
Christoffel-symbol families are those in (b)-(d).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
on $U$, for all $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

**(c) Point-normal formula.** If the chart is point-normal at $p$, that is
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]), then, writing
$g_{ad,bc}:=\partial_b\partial_cg_{ad}$,
$$R_{abcd}(p)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{ad,bc}+g_{bc,ad}-g_{bd,ac}-g_{ac,bd}\bigr)(p) .$$
Equivalently, $R^a{}_{bcd}(p)=\tfrac12\,g^{ae}(p)\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cg_{ed}
+\partial_e\partial_dg_{bc}-\partial_e\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dg_{ec}\bigr)(p)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. That $R_{abcd}$ are the components of a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor
field and that $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth
symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field, so that the contractions above are
basis-independent and do not depend on the chart, is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(d); the Ricci symmetry
is part of that statement.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ be as in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Then the following
identities hold for all indices $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ and at every point of
every smooth chart:

**(a) Skew-symmetries.** $R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}$ and $R_{abcd}=-R_{abdc}$.
Equivalently, for smooth vector fields,
$$g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=-g\bigl(R(X,Y)W,Z\bigr) \quad\text{and}\quad g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=-g\bigl(R(Y,X)Z,W\bigr).$$

**(b) Exchange of the index pairs.** $R_{abcd}=R_{cdab}$, equivalently
$g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=g\bigl(R(Z,W)X,Y\bigr)$.

**(c) First Bianchi identity.** $R_{a[bcd]}=0$, that is,
$$R_{abcd}+R_{acdb}+R_{adbc}=0 .$$

**(d) Ricci symmetry.** $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ba}$;
consequently the Einstein tensor is symmetric, $G_{ab}=G_{ba}$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. That $R_{abcd}$ are the components of a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor
field and that $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth
symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field, so that the contractions above are
basis-independent and do not depend on the chart, is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(d); the Ricci symmetry
is part of that statement.

For $X,Y\in T_pM$, the **Ricci curvature** is

$$\operatorname{Ric}_p(X,Y):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(Z\longmapsto R_p(Z,X)Y\bigr).$$

The trace is the basis-independent trace of this endomorphism of $T_pM$; no
orthonormal basis is part of the definition. Equivalently, Ricci contracts the
first input of the curvature endomorphism with its output. The next lemma
proves smoothness and symmetry and derives the orthonormal-basis formula.

On a zero-dimensional tangent space the endomorphism and its empty trace are
zero. On an empty manifold this is the unique empty two-tensor, and the same
pointwise definition applies in dimension one and at a boundary point. No
choice of bases over the points of $M$ is made.

This item assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, namely [[def-countable-choice|countable choice]]. In the propagated dependency chain, that assumption is required through [[thm-algebraic-symmetries-of-the-riemann-tensor]]; after those interfaces are fixed, the remaining local or finite argument makes no additional countable-family choice.

Ricci curvature is a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor. For every
orthonormal basis $(e_1,\ldots,e_n)$ of $T_pM$,

$$\operatorname{Ric}_p(X,Y)=\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Rm}_p(e_i,X,Y,e_i),$$

and the value is independent of the basis.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

Let $(I,\Sigma,\gamma,k,a)$ be an FLRW model datum with conversion constant
$c>0$, with spacetime $M=I\times\Sigma$, metric $g$ and comoving congruence
$n=c^{-1}\partial_t$ ([[def-gr-flrw-model-data]]), and let $\nabla$ be the
metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Let
$(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ be a product chart with $x^0=t$, where $(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ is
a smooth chart of $\Sigma$, and let ${}^{(3)}\Gamma^i{}_{jk}$ be the Christoffel symbols of
the Riemannian metric $\gamma$ in that three-dimensional chart
([[prop-christoffel-formula-for-the-levi-civita-connection]]). Write
$\dot a$ for the derivative of the scale factor and $H=\dot a/a$ for the
Hubble parameter. Then in the product chart the Christoffel symbols
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) are:

**(a)** $\Gamma^0{}_{00}=\Gamma^0{}_{0i}=\Gamma^0{}_{i0}=0$ and
$\Gamma^i{}_{00}=0$ for $i=1,2,3$;

**(b)** $\Gamma^0{}_{ij}=\Gamma^0{}_{ji}=\dfrac{a\dot a}{c^2}\,\gamma_{ij}$
for $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$;

**(c)** $\Gamma^i{}_{0j}=\Gamma^i{}_{j0}=H\,\delta^i{}_j$ for
$i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$;

**(d)** $\Gamma^i{}_{jk}={}^{(3)}\Gamma^i{}_{jk}$ for
$i,j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$.

All components not listed vanish; equivalently, the only potentially nonzero
Christoffel-symbol families are those in (b)-(d).

This item assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as inherited through
[[def-constant-sectional-curvature-and-space-form]]; the pointwise tensor
arguments below use no further choice principle
([[def-countable-choice]]).

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold and let $\gamma$ be a Riemannian
metric on $\Sigma$ ([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]), with
curvature operator $R$, Riemann four-tensor $\operatorname{Rm}$
([[def-riemann-curvature-four-tensor]]), Ricci curvature
$\operatorname{Ric}$ ([[def-ricci-curvature]]) and scalar curvature $S$
([[def-scalar-curvature]]). Let $k\in\mathbb R$. The following three
statements are equivalent:

**(a)** The metric $\gamma$ has constant sectional curvature $k$: every
tangent two-plane has sectional curvature $k$
([[def-constant-sectional-curvature-and-space-form]],
[[def-sectional-curvature]]).

**(b)** $\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma)=2k\gamma$ at every point of $\Sigma$; that
is the curvature condition for the real parameter $k$. When $\Sigma$ is
connected and boundaryless and $k\in\{-1,0,1\}$, it is precisely the
normalized spatial-model condition of [[def-gr-flrw-spatial-model]].

**(c)** $R(X,Y)Z=k\bigl(\gamma(Y,Z)X-\gamma(X,Z)Y\bigr)$ for all smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on $\Sigma$
([[prop-curvature-tensor-of-constant-sectional-curvature]]).

Whenever these hold, the scalar curvature is $S=6k$, and the trace-free Ricci
tensor vanishes, $\operatorname{Ric}_0=0$
([[def-kulkarni-nomizu-product-trace-free-ricci-and-weyl-curvature]]).

For $X,Y\in T_pM$, the **Ricci curvature** is

$$\operatorname{Ric}_p(X,Y):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(Z\longmapsto R_p(Z,X)Y\bigr).$$

The trace is the basis-independent trace of this endomorphism of $T_pM$; no
orthonormal basis is part of the definition. Equivalently, Ricci contracts the
first input of the curvature endomorphism with its output. The next lemma
proves smoothness and symmetry and derives the orthonormal-basis formula.

On a zero-dimensional tangent space the endomorphism and its empty trace are
zero. On an empty manifold this is the unique empty two-tensor, and the same
pointwise definition applies in dimension one and at a boundary point. No
choice of bases over the points of $M$ is made.

A **Riemannian metric** on a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold $M$ is a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor $g$ such that $g_p(v,v)>0$ for every point $p$ and every nonzero $v\in T_pM$. A **Riemannian manifold** is the pair $(M,g)$.

This is a [[def-smooth-tensor-field]] giving a [[def-smooth-bundle-metric]] on $TM$. Dimension zero is allowed: its zero bilinear form is positive definite because there are no nonzero vectors. The empty manifold has its unique empty metric. Boundaries are allowed where stated, with smoothness understood up to the boundary.

This item assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through the tangent-bundle and
manifold-product suppliers cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]); no further
choice principle is used.

**(a) Data.** Let $c>0$ be a real constant. An **FLRW model datum with
conversion constant $c$** is a tuple

$$(I,\Sigma,\gamma,k,a)$$

consisting of:

1. a nonempty open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, the **time interval**
   ([[def-interval]]);
2. a spatial model datum $(\Sigma,\gamma,k)$: a connected smooth
   three-manifold $\Sigma$ without boundary, a Riemannian metric $\gamma$ on
   $\Sigma$, and a normalized curvature parameter $k\in\{-1,0,1\}$ with
   $\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma)=2k\gamma$
   ([[def-gr-flrw-spatial-model]], [[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]],
   [[def-smooth-manifold]]);
3. a **scale factor**: a smooth map $a:I\to(0,\infty)$, with values in the open
   interval of strictly positive reals
   ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]).

Its **spacetime** is the product manifold $M:=I\times\Sigma$ with the product
smooth structure
([[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]]),
a smooth four-manifold without boundary. We write $t:M\to I$ for the first
coordinate function, the **cosmic time**, and $\dot a:=\frac{d}{dt}a$ for the
derivative of the scale factor ([[def-derivative]]).

**(b) The FLRW metric.** In product charts $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with $x^0=t$,
where $(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ is a smooth chart of $\Sigma$, define the component functions

$$g_{00}:=-c^2,\qquad g_{0i}:=g_{i0}:=0,\qquad g_{ij}:=a(t)^2\gamma_{ij},\qquad i,j\in\{1,2,3\}.$$

These functions are smooth on the chart domain, and they define a smooth
symmetric covariant two-tensor field $g$ on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]): the component transformation
law is that of a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor because the definitions agree on
chart overlaps, the time component is constant and the spatial components are
multiplied by the common smooth factor $a(t)^2$. The field $g$ is the
**FLRW metric** of the datum; we write the standard informal display
$g=-c^2\,dt^2+a(t)^2\,\gamma$, meaning the symmetric tensor $-c^2\,dt\otimes dt+a(t)^2\gamma$.
That $g$ is a Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ and that the coordinate field $\partial_t$ is a time
orientation for it are not asserted by this definition but proved in
[[lem-gr-flrw-metric-and-comoving-data]] on this page; the same holds for the
clauses below that use the metric's causal classification.

**(c) Comoving congruence and cosmic time direction.** The **comoving
congruence** of the datum is the smooth vector field
$n:=c^{-1}\partial_t$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). By
[[lem-gr-flrw-metric-and-comoving-data]] the field $n$ is a smooth
future-directed unit timelike field, $g(n,n)=-1$, and the **comoving
observers** of the datum are its maximal integral curves; in product
coordinates the integral curve through $(t_0,x)$ is
$s\mapsto(t_0+s/c,x)$ on $c(I-t_0)$. Its proper-time parametrization is the
**comoving curve** $t\mapsto(t,x)$ on $I$, with constant spatial coordinate
$x\in\Sigma$ and velocity $U=cn=\partial_t$.

**(d) Hubble parameter and expansion.** The **Hubble parameter** of the datum
is the smooth function

$$H:=\frac{\dot a}{a}:I\to\mathbb R .$$

No field equation, no matter content, no equation of state, no measured value
and no claim about nature is part of this definition: an FLRW model datum is a
geometric object, and the physical reading of $c$, of $t$ as a clock reading,
of $n$ as the matter rest congruence and of $H$ as an expansion rate is
recorded in the physical postulates of the framework, not here.

Throughout, $\mathbb{R}$ is the complete ordered field
([[def-complete-ordered-field]]), neighbourhoods are those of
[[def-neighbourhood-r]] and limit points those of [[def-limit-point-r]].

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $c \in A$ be a
**limit point of $A$**. The **difference quotient of $f$ at $c$** is the function

$$q_{f,c} : A \setminus \{c\} \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad q_{f,c}(x) := \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c} .$$

The division is legitimate at every point of the domain, since $x \ne c$ gives
$x - c \ne 0$.

**The point $c$ is a limit point of $A \setminus \{c\}$, not merely of $A$.**
For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ the punctured neighbourhood
$N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c)$ omits $c$, so

$$N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c) \cap A \;=\; N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c) \cap (A \setminus \{c\}) ,$$

and the left-hand side is nonempty because $c$ is a limit point of $A$. So
$q_{f,c}$ is a function on a set having $c$ as a limit point, and
$\lim_{x \to c} q_{f,c}(x)$ is a notion that [[def-function-limit]] defines.

$f$ is **differentiable at $c$** when that limit exists, and then the
**derivative of $f$ at $c$** is

$$f'(c) \;:=\; \lim_{x \to c} q_{f,c}(x) \;=\; \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c} .$$

**Two obligations are carried by that notation, and both are discharged here.**

1. **Uniqueness.** Writing $f'(c)$ treats the right-hand side as a name for a
   single real number. That is legitimate: $c$ is a limit point of the domain
   $A \setminus \{c\}$ of $q_{f,c}$, so at most one real can satisfy the
   $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition, by [[lem-function-limit-unique]] applied to
   $q_{f,c}$. Two reals both meeting the condition are therefore equal, and the
   symbol denotes.
2. **Meaningfulness.** The hypothesis that $c$ is a limit point of $A$ is not
   decoration. At an **isolated** point of $A$ the punctured condition
   $0 < |x - c| < \delta$ is met by no point of the domain at all, so the

derivations.claim: (The $\operatorname{Ric}_{00}$ component.) By [L3], $\operatorname{Ric}_{00}=\sum_cR^c{}_{0c0}$. In the sum, the term $c=0$ is $R^0{}_{000}=0$ because every term of [L2] contains a symbol $\Gamma^{\cdot}{}_{00}$ or $\Gamma^0{}_{0\cdot}$, all of which vanish by [L1]. For $c=i$ the same formula gives $R^i{}_{0i0}=\partial_i\Gamma^i{}_{00}-\partial_0\Gamma^i{}_{i0}+\sum_e(\Gamma^i{}_{ie}\Gamma^e{}_{00}-\Gamma^i{}_{0e}\Gamma^e{}_{i0})=0-\dot H-\sum_e\Gamma^i{}_{0e}\Gamma^e{}_{i0}$, using $\Gamma^i{}_{00}=0$ and $\Gamma^i{}_{i0}=H\delta^i{}_i=H$ from [L1]; the remaining quadratic term is $-\sum_e\Gamma^i{}_{0e}\Gamma^e{}_{i0}=-\sum_m(H\delta^i{}_m)(H\delta^m{}_i)=-H^2$, because the terms with $e=0$ contain the vanishing symbol $\Gamma^0{}_{i0}$. Summing over $c=0,1,2,3$ gives $\operatorname{Ric}_{00}=3(-\dot H-H^2)=-3\ddot a/a$, where $\dot H=\ddot a/a-(\dot a/a)^2=\ddot a/a-H^2$ by [L6].

(The spatial components.) By [L3], $\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=\sum_cR^c{}_{icj}=R^0{}_{i0j}+\sum_kR^k{}_{ikj}$. For the term $c=0$, [L2] and [L1] give $R^0{}_{i0j}=\partial_0\Gamma^0{}_{ji}-\partial_j\Gamma^0{}_{0i}+\sum_e(\Gamma^0{}_{0e}\Gamma^e{}_{ji}-\Gamma^0{}_{je}\Gamma^e{}_{0i})=\partial_0\bigl(a\dot a\gamma_{ij}/c^2\bigr)+0-\sum_m\bigl(a\dot a\gamma_{jm}/c^2\bigr)\bigl(H\delta^m{}_i\bigr)$, since $\Gamma^0{}_{0e}=0$ and $\Gamma^0{}_{je}=0$ for $e=0$; with $\partial_0(a\dot a)=a\ddot a+\dot a^2$ and $a\dot aH=\dot a^2$ this is $\bigl(a\ddot a+\dot a^2-\dot a^2\bigr)\gamma_{ij}/c^2=a\ddot a\gamma_{ij}/c^2$. For the spatial terms, substituting [L1] into [L2] and summing over $k$ separates the $\gamma$-symbols from the time-dependent symbols exactly as in the third family of [[lem-gr-flrw-christoffel-symbols]]: the terms with some index $0$ contribute the total $3Ha\dot a\gamma_{ij}/c^2-Ha\dot a\gamma_{ij}/c^2=2\dot a^2\gamma_{ij}/c^2$, and the remaining terms are $\sum_k\bigl(\partial_k{}^{(3)}\Gamma^k{}_{ji}-\partial_j{}^{(3)}\Gamma^k{}_{ki}+\sum_m({}^{(3)}\Gamma^k{}_{km}{}^{(3)}\Gamma^m{}_{ji}-{}^{(3)}\Gamma^k{}_{jm}{}^{(3)}\Gamma^m{}_{ki})\bigr)=\sum_k{}^{(3)}R^k{}_{ikj}=2k\gamma_{ij}$ by [L5]. For $c=j$, [L2] and [L1] give $R^j{}_{0ji}=\partial_j\Gamma^j{}_{i0}-\partial_i\Gamma^j{}_{j0}+\sum_e(\Gamma^j{}_{je}\Gamma^e{}_{i0}-\Gamma^j{}_{ie}\Gamma^e{}_{j0})=0-0+\sum_m\bigl({}^{(3)}\Gamma^j{}_{jm}H\delta^m{}_i-{}^{(3)}\Gamma^j{}_{im}H\delta^m{}_j\bigr)$, since the terms with $e=0$ contain $\Gamma^0{}_{i0}=\Gamma^0{}_{j0}=0$ and the spatial derivatives of the functions $H(t)\delta^j{}_i$ vanish; substituting $\delta^m{}_i$ and $\delta^m{}_j$ and summing over $j$ gives $H\sum_j({}^{(3)}\Gamma^j{}_{ji}-{}^{(3)}\Gamma^j{}_{ij})=0$ by the symmetry of the spatial symbols. By [L3] and [L4], $S=g^{00}\operatorname{Ric}_{00}+g^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=-c^{-2}\bigl(-3\ddot a/a\bigr)+a^{-2}\gamma^{ij}\bigl(\tfrac{a\ddot a+2\dot a^2}{c^2}\gamma_{ij}+2k\gamma_{ij}\bigr)$. **(a) Data.** A **Friedmann-system datum** is a tuple

$$(c,G_N,\Lambda,I,k,a,\varepsilon,p)$$

consisting of positive real constants $c>0$ and $G_N>0$, a real constant
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, a nonempty open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$
([[def-interval]]), a real number $k$ (the **curvature parameter** of the
datum), and smooth functions $a:I\to(0,\infty)$, $\varepsilon:I\to\mathbb R$
and $p:I\to\mathbb R$, with values in the open interval of strictly positive
reals in the case of $a$
([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). We write
$\dot a,\ddot a,\dot\varepsilon$ for the derivatives of these functions of one
variable and

$$H:=\frac{\dot a}{a}:I\to\mathbb R$$

for the **Hubble parameter** of the datum ([[def-derivative]]). No relation
between $k$ and the three signs $\{-1,0,1\}$ is imposed by this definition;
the spatial model data of [[def-gr-flrw-model-data]] restrict to those signs,
and the real parameter is used so that the equations can also be examined
after a rescaling of the spatial metric.

**(b) The equations.** For a Friedmann-system datum define the following three
scalar equations on $I$:

**(F) The Friedmann equation.**

$$H(t)^2+\frac{kc^2}{a(t)^2}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{3c^2}\,\varepsilon(t)+\frac{\Lambda c^2}{3}\qquad\text{for all }t\in I;$$

**(A) The acceleration equation.**

$$\frac{\ddot a(t)}{a(t)}=-\frac{4\pi G_N}{3c^2}\bigl(\varepsilon(t)+3p(t)\bigr)+\frac{\Lambda c^2}{3}\qquad\text{for all }t\in I;$$

**(C) The continuity equation.**

$$\dot\varepsilon(t)+3H(t)\bigl(\varepsilon(t)+p(t)\bigr)=0\qquad\text{for all }t\in I .$$

We also record the **spatial-component equation**

**(S)**

$$-\frac{2a(t)\ddot a(t)+\dot a(t)^2}{c^2}-k+\Lambda a(t)^2=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}\,p(t)\,a(t)^2\qquad\text{for all }t\in I .$$

Each of (F), (A), (C), (S) is an equality of real numbers at each point of
$I$; the equations involve the data of clause (a) alone. Their relation to the
curvature components of an FLRW metric, and their logical relations among one
another, are the content of the results on this page and are not asserted by
this definition. In particular, this definition adopts no equation of state:
a relation $p=P(\varepsilon)$, when used, is an additional datum.

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $c \in A$ be a limit point of $A$
([[def-limit-point-r]]), let $f, g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $c$
([[def-derivative]]) and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then:

1. $f + g$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(f+g)'(c) = f'(c) + g'(c)$;
2. $\alpha f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(\alpha f)'(c) = \alpha f'(c)$;
3. $fg$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(fg)'(c) = f'(c)g(c) + f(c)g'(c)$;
4. if $g(c) \ne 0$ then, writing $A_0 := \{\, x \in A : g(x) \ne 0 \,\}$, the
   point $c$ lies in $A_0$ and is a limit point of $A_0$, the quotient
   $(f/g)|_{A_0} : A_0 \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x)/g(x)$, is differentiable
   at $c$ as a function on $A_0$, and
   $$\bigl((f/g)|_{A_0}\bigr)'(c) \;=\; \frac{f'(c)\,g(c) - f(c)\,g'(c)}{g(c)^{2}} .$$

it has the stated value. Both are proved.

vanishes, and $g$ may vanish at points of $A$ far from $c$; restricting to $A_0$
is forced. That the restriction still has $c$ as a limit point, so that a
derivative there means anything at all, is not free either, and it is the last
claim of [[lem-sign-preservation-near-a-limit]] applied to $g$. The hypothesis
is $g(c) \ne 0$, not "$g$ vanishes nowhere".

**Everything is proved through
[[thm-caratheodory-characterisation]].** No difference quotient is estimated and
no limit theorem beyond continuity is used, so no choice principle is spent.
The four identities are four algebraic rearrangements of an increment, each
followed by a reading of [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]].

Let $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$g[A] \subseteq B$ and let $f : B \to \mathbb{R}$, so that the composite
$f \circ g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined. Let $c \in A$ be a limit point of
$A$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]) at which $g$ is differentiable
([[def-derivative]]), put $b := g(c)$, and suppose $b$ is a limit point of $B$

isolated point of $B$, and there $f'(b)$ is not defined and the formula asserts

arbitrarily close to $c$. Carathéodory's factorisation never divides by the
inner increment, so the difficulty does not arise.

([[def-complete-ordered-field]]), neighbourhoods are those of
[[def-neighbourhood-r]] and limit points those of [[def-limit-point-r]].

**limit point of $A$**. The **difference quotient of $f$ at $c$** is the function
